About
Fermata is an agricultural technology company based in Israel and Toronto, Canada, that develops AI-powered computer vision solutions to automate the early detection of pests and diseases in commercial crops. The company's core software platform, Croptimus, utilizes continuous image analysis from specialized cameras to monitor both greenhouse and outdoor cultivation environments. By implementing this automated technology, commercial growers can reduce overall crop loss by 30 percent and decrease their manual monitoring time by 50 percent. Fermata has raised $10 million in venture capital funding to scale its operations, with its most recent investment round led by Raw Ventures. The enterprise provides software subscription services to various licensed producers and agricultural clients, including Mariwell, and has participated in the StartLife accelerator program. The organization was founded in 2019 by Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree Valeria Kogan.

Fermata, an innovative agtech startup, has raised $10 million in Series A funding from Raw Ventures. This investment aims to transform precision agriculture by leveraging AI and data analytics. With its state-of-the-art computer vision technology, Fermata’s Croptimus platform allows farmers to identify pests and diseases early, remarkably minimizing crop losses.

Fermata’s Innovations in Crop Management and Farming Solutions
Fermata leads the way in data science and computer vision for agriculture, recently securing $10 million in a Series A funding round from Raw Ventures. This investment will help us develop a centralized digital brain for the horticulture industry, remarkably improving crop management and farming solutions. As global food demand surges and weather patterns become increasingly erratic, our innovations in precision agriculture and data analytics are critical.
Our flagship platform, Croptimus™, utilizes AI and machine learning to continuously monitor crops. It detects pests and diseases early, potentially reducing crop loss by up to 30%. This technology enhances agricultural efficiency and promotes sustainability by minimizing chemical usage. We are dedicated to advancing Croptimus™ with features like yield optimization and irrigation management.
By harnessing automation and robotics, we aim to transform agriculture. Our partnerships with industry leaders, including AI advancements, keep us at the forefront of innovation. Fermata is committed to tackling current challenges while shaping the future of agriculture for generations to come.
Role of Robotics and Automation in Fermata’s Technology Strategy
Fermata’s recent $10 million Series A funding accelerates our technology strategy, focusing on the integration of robotics and automation in agriculture. This investment supports our vision of a centralized digital brain for the horticulture industry, enhancing precision agriculture with AI and machine learning.
Our flagship platform, Croptimus™, utilizes computer vision to monitor crops continuously. This advanced system automates pest and disease detection, enabling farmers to respond quickly. By leveraging real-time data analytics, we empower growers to refine their crop management strategies.
Key benefits of our approach include:
 Efficiency: Automation reduces manual labor, allowing farmers to focus on strategic decisions.
 Sustainability: Our technology minimizes chemical use, promoting environmentally friendly practices.
 Data-Driven Insights: Advanced analytics provide actionable intelligence for enhanced crop yields.
Fermata is revolutionizing agriculture through our commitment to innovation and sustainability, paving the way for a smarter future in farming.
Future Growth and Sustainability Goals Post-Funding
Fermata’s recent $10 million Series A funding is a pivotal moment for the future of agriculture. This investment accelerates our development of AI-driven technologies designed for precision agriculture. Our goal is to create a centralized digital brain that leverages data analytics and machine learning, providing farmers worldwide with powerful tools.
Following this funding, we are committed to achieving key sustainability goals:
 Environmental Impact: Automating pest detection reduces chemical use, promoting sustainable farming.
 Food Security: Our technology enhances crop yields, addressing global food demand challenges.
 Economic Development: We aim to create jobs in the agritech sector, driving innovation and economic growth.
With advanced robotics and automation, Fermata is set to lead the smart farming transformation. Our Croptimus™ platform exemplifies this commitment, offering real-time insights to farmers. As we refine our technology, we envision a future where agriculture thrives sustainably, adapting to the impacts of climate change.
Partnering with industry leaders, we are excited to explore new opportunities in agriculture. Together, we can transform farming practices for generations to come.
Summing up
Fermata’s recent $10 million funding accelerates our journey towards sustainable agriculture. This investment will improve our technology and expand our impact on crop management. By harnessing AI and computer vision, we empower farmers to grow healthier crops while reducing waste. Our goal is profitability by 2026, underscoring our dedication to long-term food security and environmental health.

The Frontier Psychiatrists
Radial Launches with $50 Million to Expand Access to Advanced Brain Medicine
Or, How a Quixotic Substack Plus The Team From Amazon Pharmacy Turned Into a Company.
Owen Scott Muir, M.D.
It is not every day I get to write what follows! The Frontier Psychiatrists newsletter has had a point of view over the years—new treatments that modulate brain circuits are better for human suffering than now-ancient medicines. Broad insurance coverage for them should be a goal for a professional enterprise.
This is a quixotic point of view, I grant you, dear readers. Owen Muir—a child and adult psychiatrist—is the editor and author of most of this newsletter, and…hold on, I’m going to slip into first-person narration here—it’s just easier.
The Frontier Psychiatrists was actually created by Carlene MacMillan, M.D., DFAACAP, FCTMSS. She and I had created a company called Brooklyn Minds, which we exited from when she got the tech bug and joined Osmind as their Chief Medical Officer. I have been banging the drum about getting someone to pay for treatments like Accelerated TMS for years, but before an FDA label, it just wasn’t believable as a company. There have been some false starts. I even wrote, eloquently, I thought, about why no one should raise money for healthcare companies.
Well, it turns out people who disagreed with me about the futility of fundraising were reading what I was writing. Maybe my ideas about how we need Visionary Healthcare Leadership were landing with people who knew a thing or two about venture-scalable healthcare? (circa July, 2022):
> With the acquisition of One Medical by Amazon, whether the public knows it or not, a massive change is taking place in the tech-enabled and capital-inefficient healthcare landscape. The reason we don’t understand what the future of healthcare should look like is that we don’t have visionary leaders to explain it to us. There is no one championing the standard that we should follow.
In that article, I compared healthcare companies to Amazon:
> [Amazon]…That IS a market cap measured in Trillions of Dollars. Amazon is a Real Company. And with the acquisition of One Medical for $3.9b, Amazon is a Real Company all in on bricks and fancy couches in Healthcare.
John Capecelatro and Elliot Cohen from PillPack, which Amazon acquired, built Amazon Pharmacy, and subsequently founded a new company called Radial.
Amusingly, right when my old clinic, Fermata, merged with Radial, another company also called Fermata—an AI-guided pest control company in the tech-enabled agribusiness space—announced a $10m raise. Despite having nothing to do with that, I've been getting invited to fruit logistics conferences ever since:
## Dreams of Fruit Logistics
Owen Scott Muir, M.D, DFAACAP
·
March 11, 2025
The Frontier Psychiatrists is a health-themed newsletter. However, every once in a while, there is a mixup. To be clear, fruit is healthy. At least in reasonably sized doses, fruit has soluble fiber and is generally full of vitamins and other nutrients. It's got a lot of sugar; in the case of fruit juice, it can have as much sugar as soda, and it's not generally healthy to drink gallons of sugar. Don't do that. So it is terrible for you. Fruit juice is soda without fizz. It's a health-branded soda. Don't drink sugar water.
Read full story
We built a different company. It is not about fruit logistics, but it is still pretty sweet. And there is a good deal of logistics involved. We see a future where psychiatric treatments work. They work shockingly well. Depression treatment that gets to depression to end exist. I’ve been involved in proving that point over and over. We have an embarrassment of riches when it comes to innovations that are both here, now and in the pipeline.
It’s briefly worth mentioning that The Frontier Psychiatrists is no longer shouting into a disinterested void. We have partners in the world who are pursuing similar missions—excellent clinical services organizations like Beckley Clinical, Salma, Stella Centers, Acacia Clinics, Hope Therapeutics, and “logistics only” companies like Osmind, Big Leap, and Everbright—all believe that we need to get these next generation of treatments to the world. Over 300 million dollars has gone from investors into the space. This is not a competition, as I see it. It’s a shared understanding that there is a tremendous amount of suffering to be addressed, and the only winner we want to see, collectively, is our patients.
I know most of the other companies in the space, and many include friends of many years. We will be working together both before and after whatever job we have at this very moment—medicine is a long road. People I interviewed with for residency training have come to work for me, and vice versa.
Let's me paint a quick picture of the size of the problem we are seeking to address: 80% of people will have a neuropsychiatric illness in their lifetime. 13% of teenage girls and 7% of teenage boys will attempt suicide in the US—and that was 2023 data. 20% of girls and 5% of boys will be victims of sexual abuse in childhood, which reliably leads to PTSD and other psychiatric problems.
We are talking about millions and millions of people who deserve help—and those numbers were just about youth. The problems don’t stop in youth, they tend to continue, and becomes more complex and serious as we age—and “band aids” likely cannabis actually make the problems worse for older adults:
## Does Cannabis Cause Dementia and Kill You?
Owen Scott Muir, M.D, DFAACAP
·
April 22, 2025
The Frontier Psychiatrists is a newsletter that addresses health-themed material. It’s written by Owen Scott Muir, M.D., DFAACAP, who practices at Fermata in NYC, Acacia Clinics in Sunnyvale, CA, and at Living Water in Myrtle Beach, CA.
Read full story
The pills weren’t working. Regular old therapy is good, but both not always effective, and hard to scale up because it requires human connection and skill, not chatbots cos-playing as therapists.
1 in 5 people will eventually get cancer. 1 in 5 girls will be sexually abused before they reach adulthood. Are we getting it? Trauma, grief, loss, addiction, and the inability to attain profound and meaningful healing can’t be how we go about our lives, but it’s the standard with which we now live. Half-measures grimly accepted, and hopelessness as our North Star? Not anymore.
What changes this regrettable state of affairs? Well, it’s a few things:
1. Recognition of the problem
2. Awareness that solutions—not just half-measures—exit for our suffering.
3. Payment models that pay for the best treatments first.
4. The technology to provide these treatments at massive scale.
5. The technology to determine what treatment is best for which human.
6. And a streamlined path for the next best and safest treatments to get into the above system.
We did this with cars—the car itself worked, then we needed gas stations, roads, highways, toll booths, maps, GPS, EVs, chargers—but no one accepts that they could never hope to go from Boston to New Haven because it’s just too far to walk.
At Radial, we are doing it for human suffering. Without further ado, our press release:
Radial Launches with $50 Million to Expand Access to Advanced Brain Medicine
NEW YORK, NY — December 9, 2025 — Radial today announced the company has raised $50 million in venture funding to create access to the world’s most advanced mental health treatments. The company is backed by General Catalyst, who led the Series A, and additional investors Solari Capital, JSL Health Capital, Founder Collective, BoxGroup, Scrub Capital, and Diede van Lamoen.
New brain medicines – treatments like neuromodulation (e.g. accelerated transcranial magnetic stimulation, (TMS)) and rapid-acting medications (e.g. Spravato) that directly heal the brain – are achieving far better outcomes for patients with mental health conditions. These treatments work in days to weeks, with some studies showing remission rates as high as 78%. However, the current healthcare system is designed to deliver long-term medication-based management, not the more episodic interventional brain medicine supported by modern evidence. Further, the system does not measure outcomes, which limits payors ability to pay for the best care possible, and nor do clinicians have the best clinical decision support and operational tools to enable these new forms of care at scale.
Radial is addressing this problem for patients, providers, and payers by developing clinical infrastructure, reimbursement tools, and decision support that’s designed around modern brain medicine. The company is building a national network of clinics that accept most major forms of insurance, including Medicare,Tricare, VA-CCN, Aetna, Cigna, United, and many Blues plans. For patients this means the most effective combination of therapies are available to everyone who needs them, for clinicians this means focusing on providing that care, and for payors this means better outcomes and less ultimate cost for even the most complex patients.
John Capecelatro, CEO and co-founder of Radial commented, “People who are struggling with mental health can’t wait years to see if something might help through trial and error. New rapid-acting treatments work in days or weeks instead of years. We’re seeing remission rates for depression of 50-60% and as high as 78% in some studies our team has co-authored. The healthcare system hasn’t caught up. Radial is here to change that. When we have tools for the right clinical workflows and insurance pathways, people can access therapies that help them get better far sooner. It’s a dramatic difference for individuals, for families, and for the health system that ends up carrying the cost when care drags on without results.”
“Psychiatry is undergoing a transformation, but most of that progress hasn’t reached patients. The science is there, yet the infrastructure to deliver modern, brain-based treatments at scale is still missing,” said Reva Nohria, Partner at General Catalyst. “Radial understands both the clinical evidence and the operational complexity required to close that gap. We believe this work can meaningfully expand access to effective mental health care.”
“In research, we’ve proven that these powerful treatments work. They change lives. The hard part has always been bringing them into everyday clinical practice. Radial was built to close that gap. We’re taking what we know from years of clinical research and turning it into care that any patient can access. Radial is focused on the care patients have long deserved.” added Owen Muir, Chief Medical Officer at Radial.
Radial currently operates with seven clinics in six states, supported by its proprietary software platform. This fundraising will support the company’s plans to expand nationally in 2026, growing both its clinic network and technology partnerships.
About Radial
Yesterday Morning…
Radial is expanding access to the world’s most advanced mental health treatments by Radial is developing clinical infrastructure, reimbursement tools, and AI-guided decision support designed around novel psychiatry treatments like neuromodulation (e.g. TMS), medication (e.g. Spravato), and other interventional therapies. Their goal is to make transformative care accessible to all. Learn more at www.meetradial.com.

What's the long term remission like? Call me cynical, but I find it hard to believe that a quick fix that leaves the patient's social situation (crappy job, abusive partner, substance abusing children, demented parents needing care) unchanged is going to have long term effectiveness. Most so called depression is life difficulties, social and situational. It'll take a lot to convince me that a solution that completely ignores the social context is the answer.
I get it is possibly effective for melancholia, the traditional endogenous depression, and that's where it could be life-changing, but most depression diagnosed nowadays is life difficulties (eg every teenager with an adjustment disorder is told they have depression by primary care).
